description: Metformin is the most commonly prescribed medication for type 2 diabetes. It lowers the amount of sugar your liver releases into your blood and helps your body respond better to insulin.
howItWorks: Metformin works in three ways: it reduces the amount of glucose produced by your liver, it slows the absorption of sugar from your intestines, and it helps your muscle cells use insulin more effectively. It does not cause your body to produce more insulin, which is why it rarely causes dangerously low blood sugar on its own.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food. Symptoms usually improve as your body adjusts.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common when starting or increasing dose
commonSideEffects.advice: Start with a low dose and increase gradually. Drink plenty of water.
This is harmless and usually goes away on its own.
Eat regular small meals even if you do not feel hungry.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Lactic acidosis (very rare): unusual muscle pain, difficulty breathing, stomach pain, feeling cold, dizziness
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking metformin and go to the hospital immediately. This is rare but serious.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical help immediately.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Drinking alcohol while taking metformin increases the risk of lactic acidosis and can cause dangerously low blood sugar.
Bitter gourd can lower blood sugar on its own. Combining it with metformin may cause blood sugar to drop too low.

description: Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker used to treat high blood pressure. It relaxes your blood vessels so blood can flow more easily, reducing the strain on your heart.
howItWorks: Amlodipine blocks calcium from entering the muscle cells of your heart and blood vessels. When calcium is blocked, the blood vessels relax and widen, allowing blood to flow through more easily. This lowers your blood pressure and reduces the workload on your heart. The effect builds up over 7-10 days.

commonSideEffects.advice: Elevate your feet when sitting. This is not dangerous but tell your doctor if it bothers you.
Usually improves as your body adjusts. Take a mild painkiller if needed.
This is caused by blood vessels widening. It is not harmful.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Occasional, especially when standing up quickly
commonSideEffects.advice: Stand up slowly from sitting or lying down. Avoid driving if you feel dizzy.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Very fast or irregular heartbeat
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek medical attention immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe dizziness or fainting
seriousSideEffects.action: Lie down and call your doctor. If it happens repeatedly, go to the hospital.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Grapefruit can increase the amount of amlodipine in your blood, making side effects worse.
This herbal supplement can reduce the effectiveness of amlodipine, causing your blood pressure to rise.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you notice significant ankle swelling that does not improve, persistent headaches, or if your blood pressure readings remain high despite taking amlodipine regularly.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-30 degrees Celsius. Keep away from moisture. Store in the original blister pack until ready to take. Do not refrigerate.

description: Losartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) that treats high blood pressure. It blocks a chemical in your body that causes blood vessels to tighten, helping them relax and lowering blood pressure.
howItWorks: Losartan blocks the action of angiotensin II, a hormone that normally causes blood vessels to narrow. By blocking this hormone at its receptor, losartan allows blood vessels to relax and widen. It also reduces the amount of water and salt your kidneys retain, further lowering blood pressure. It provides kidney-protective benefits for people with diabetes.

commonSideEffects.advice: Stand up slowly. Avoid driving until you know how losartan affects you.
Mild cold-like symptoms may occur. See your doctor if they persist.
Stay hydrated and stretch regularly. Tell your doctor if pain is severe.

commonSideEffects.advice: This usually improves as your body adjusts to the medication.

seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor immediately. High potassium can be dangerous.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of kidney problems: changes in urination amount, swelling in feet or ankles
seriousSideEffects.action: See your doctor as soon as possible for blood tests.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Losartan can raise potassium levels. Adding more potassium can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems.
Regular use of these painkillers can reduce the blood pressure lowering effect of losartan and harm your kidneys.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you experience swelling of your face, lips, or tongue, difficulty breathing, or if you notice a significant decrease in the amount of urine you pass.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-30 degrees Celsius. Keep in the original container, tightly closed. Protect from light. Do not store in humid environments like the bathroom.

description: Atorvastatin is a statin medication used to lower cholesterol levels and reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke. It is one of the most widely prescribed medications for people with diabetes or hypertension who have elevated cholesterol.
howItWorks: Atorvastatin works by blocking an enzyme in your liver called HMG-CoA reductase, which your body uses to make cholesterol. By reducing cholesterol production, atorvastatin lowers the levels of LDL (bad) cholesterol and triglycerides in your blood while slightly raising HDL (good) cholesterol. It also helps stabilise existing fatty deposits in your blood vessels, reducing the risk of them breaking off and causing a heart attack or stroke.

commonSideEffects.advice: Mild muscle aches are usually harmless. Stay active and stretch regularly. Tell your doctor if pain is persistent or severe.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common in the first few weeks
commonSideEffects.advice: Usually improves as your body adjusts. A mild painkiller can help.
Take with food if stomach upset occurs. Symptoms usually settle within a few days.
Try taking atorvastatin in the morning instead of at night if this occurs.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially with fever or dark urine (rhabdomyolysis)
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking atorvastatin and seek emergency medical attention immediately. This is rare but can cause kidney damage.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent nausea, upper stomach pain
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor immediately. Liver function tests may be needed.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Grapefruit inhibits the enzyme that breaks down atorvastatin, increasing drug levels in your blood and raising the risk of side effects including muscle damage.
This herbal supplement speeds up the breakdown of atorvastatin in your liver, potentially making it ineffective at controlling your cholesterol.
Heavy alcohol use combined with atorvastatin increases the risk of liver damage. Limit alcohol to occasional small amounts.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor urgently if you experience unexplained muscle pain or weakness, especially if accompanied by fever, dark-coloured urine, or general tiredness. Also seek help if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-25 degrees Celsius. Keep in the original packaging to protect from moisture. Do not store above 30 degrees Celsius. Keep out of direct sunlight.

description: Glibenclamide (also known as glyburide) is a sulfonylurea medication used to treat type 2 diabetes. It stimulates your pancreas to produce more insulin, helping lower blood sugar levels after meals.
howItWorks: Glibenclamide binds to specific receptors on the insulin-producing beta cells in your pancreas, causing them to release more insulin. This extra insulin helps move sugar from your blood into your cells, lowering your blood sugar. The effect lasts most of the day, which is why it is usually taken once or twice daily.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common, especially if meals are missed
commonSideEffects.advice: Always carry glucose tablets or a sugary drink. Eat regular meals at consistent times. Symptoms include shakiness, sweating, confusion, and fast heartbeat.
Maintain a balanced diet and stay physically active. Discuss with your doctor if weight gain is significant.
Take with food. Symptoms usually improve after the first few weeks.
Tell your doctor if you develop a rash. This may indicate a sensitivity to the medication.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe low blood sugar: confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a medical emergency. If the person is conscious, give them sugar immediately. If unconscious, call for emergency help — do not try to give food or drink.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction: widespread rash, difficulty breathing, swelling of face or throat
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical help immediately.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Alcohol can cause unpredictable drops in blood sugar when combined with glibenclamide, increasing the risk of dangerous hypoglycaemia.
Glibenclamide stimulates insulin production regardless of food intake. Skipping meals while taking it can cause blood sugar to drop dangerously low.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek immediate help if you experience severe low blood sugar symptoms such as confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness. Contact your doctor if you have frequent mild low blood sugar episodes, as your dose may need adjusting.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-25 degrees Celsius. Keep in the original container, tightly closed. Protect from light and moisture.

description: Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) is a thiazide diuretic, commonly called a 'water pill'. It helps your body get rid of extra salt and water through your urine, which lowers blood pressure and reduces swelling.
howItWorks: Hydrochlorothiazide works in your kidneys by blocking the reabsorption of sodium and chloride. When these salts are passed out in your urine, water follows them, reducing the volume of fluid in your blood vessels. Less fluid means lower pressure on your vessel walls. It also relaxes blood vessels slightly over time, providing an additional blood pressure lowering effect.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Very common, especially in the first few days
commonSideEffects.advice: Take your dose in the morning to avoid night-time bathroom trips. This effect lessens as your body adjusts.
Stand up slowly from sitting or lying down. Drink adequate water throughout the day.
Eat potassium-rich foods like bananas, oranges, and spinach. Tell your doctor if cramps are frequent.
Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing when outdoors. Avoid prolonged sun exposure.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of severe electrolyte imbalance: irregular heartbeat, extreme weakness, muscle spasms, confusion
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek medical attention immediately. You may need blood tests to check your electrolyte levels.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of severe dehydration: extreme thirst, very dry mouth, little or no urination, rapid heartbeat
seriousSideEffects.action: Drink fluids and contact your doctor immediately.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: While HCTZ can lower potassium, taking too much potassium replacement without blood test monitoring can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems.
These painkillers can reduce the blood pressure lowering effect of hydrochlorothiazide and increase the risk of kidney problems.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you experience persistent muscle cramps, weakness, irregular heartbeat, or if you feel unusually thirsty or pass very little urine. Seek urgent help for signs of severe allergic reaction.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-30 degrees Celsius. Keep in the original container, tightly closed. Protect from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom.

description: Enalapril is an ACE inhibitor used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure. It relaxes blood vessels by blocking the production of a hormone that causes them to tighten, making it easier for your heart to pump blood.
howItWorks: Enalapril blocks an enzyme called angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) that produces angiotensin II, a hormone that narrows blood vessels. By reducing angiotensin II, your blood vessels relax and widen, lowering blood pressure. Enalapril also reduces the amount of water your body retains, which further helps lower blood pressure and ease the workload on your heart.

commonSideEffects.advice: This is a known side effect of all ACE inhibitors. If it becomes bothersome, talk to your doctor — they may switch you to a different type of medication.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common, especially with the first dose
commonSideEffects.advice: Take the first dose at bedtime. Stand up slowly from sitting or lying positions.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common in the first few weeks

This usually improves over the first few weeks of treatment.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat (angioedema)

seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor immediately for blood tests.

Regular use can reduce the effectiveness of enalapril and increase the risk of kidney problems.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek emergency help immediately if you experience swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or have difficulty breathing. Contact your doctor if you develop a persistent dry cough or notice changes in urination.

description: Nifedipine is a calcium channel blocker used to treat high blood pressure and angina (chest pain). It works by relaxing the blood vessels and improving blood flow, reducing the effort your heart needs to pump blood.
howItWorks: Nifedipine blocks calcium from entering the smooth muscle cells of your blood vessels. Without calcium, these muscles cannot contract as strongly, so blood vessels relax and widen. This reduces blood pressure and allows more blood and oxygen to reach your heart. The extended-release form provides steady blood pressure control throughout the day.

commonSideEffects.advice: Usually improves within the first week. A mild painkiller can help. Tell your doctor if headaches are severe.
This is caused by blood vessels widening and is not harmful. It usually decreases over time.

Stand up slowly. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how nifedipine affects you.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Very fast heartbeat or palpitations that do not settle
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek medical attention. Nifedipine can sometimes cause reflex tachycardia.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe chest pain or worsening angina
seriousSideEffects.action: Go to the hospital immediately.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Grapefruit increases the amount of nifedipine in your blood, which can cause your blood pressure to drop too low and worsen side effects.
Extended-release tablets must be swallowed whole. Crushing them releases the full dose at once, which can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you experience severe or persistent headaches, rapid heartbeat, or worsening chest pain. Seek emergency help if you feel faint or if your heartbeat becomes very irregular.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-25 degrees Celsius. Protect from light and moisture. Keep in the original packaging.

description: Insulin Glargine is a long-acting insulin used to control blood sugar levels in people with diabetes. It provides a steady, low level of insulin over 24 hours, mimicking your body's natural background insulin production.
howItWorks: Insulin Glargine is injected under the skin where it forms tiny crystals that dissolve slowly over 24 hours. This provides a steady release of insulin that helps your body process sugar between meals and overnight. Unlike rapid-acting insulins, it does not have a sharp peak, which reduces the risk of sudden low blood sugar episodes.

commonSideEffects.effect: Injection site reactions: redness, swelling, or itching
commonSideEffects.advice: Rotate injection sites between your stomach, thighs, and upper arms. Do not inject into the same spot repeatedly.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common if dose is too high or meals are skipped
commonSideEffects.advice: Always carry glucose tablets or a sugary snack. Learn to recognise symptoms: shakiness, sweating, hunger, fast heartbeat, confusion.
Maintain a balanced diet and stay physically active. Discuss with your doctor if weight gain is a concern.

commonSideEffects.effect: Lipodystrophy (lumps or dents at injection sites)
commonSideEffects.frequency: Occasional with repeated injection in same area
commonSideEffects.advice: Rotate injection sites regularly. Do not inject into lumpy areas as insulin absorption becomes unpredictable.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe low blood sugar: confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness
seriousSideEffects.action: This is an emergency. If conscious, give sugar immediately. If unconscious, do not give food — place in recovery position and call for emergency help.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction: whole-body rash, difficulty breathing, rapid heartbeat
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical help immediately. This is very rare with modern insulins.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Mixing with other insulins in the same syringe

description: Low-dose aspirin is used to help prevent heart attacks and strokes in people at high risk, including those with diabetes or hypertension. At low doses, it stops blood cells (platelets) from clumping together and forming dangerous clots.
howItWorks: Aspirin permanently blocks an enzyme called cyclooxygenase (COX) in your platelets. This prevents platelets from producing thromboxane A2, a chemical that makes platelets sticky and promotes clot formation. Since platelets cannot repair themselves, aspirin's effect lasts for the entire 7-10 day lifespan of each platelet. This is why even a small daily dose provides continuous protection against clots.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food or after eating. Enteric-coated tablets can reduce stomach irritation.
This is expected because aspirin reduces blood clotting. Bruises are usually harmless but tell your doctor about unusual bruising.
Apply pressure to stop bleeding. If bleeding is frequent or heavy, contact your doctor.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of stomach bleeding: black or tarry stools, vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, severe stomach pain
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking aspirin and seek emergency medical help immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of bleeding in the brain: sudden severe headache, confusion, vision changes, difficulty speaking, weakness on one side
seriousSideEffects.action: Call for emergency help immediately. This is very rare but serious.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Other blood thinners (warfarin, clopidogrel) without doctor supervision
avoidanceWarnings.reason: Combining blood thinners significantly increases the risk of serious bleeding. Only take together if specifically prescribed by your doctor.
Ibuprofen can block aspirin's protective heart effect if taken first. If you need both, take aspirin at least 30 minutes before ibuprofen.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek emergency help if you notice black or bloody stools, vomit blood, or have a sudden severe headache. Contact your doctor if you experience persistent stomach pain, unusual bleeding, or if you need a surgical or dental procedure (aspirin may need to be paused).
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-25 degrees Celsius. Keep dry and away from moisture. Store in the original container with the lid tightly closed.

description: Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor used to treat high blood pressure, heart failure, and to protect the kidneys in people with diabetes. It relaxes blood vessels by blocking a hormone that causes them to tighten.
howItWorks: Lisinopril blocks angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), which normally converts angiotensin I into angiotensin II — a powerful hormone that narrows blood vessels and causes your body to retain salt and water. By blocking this conversion, lisinopril allows blood vessels to relax, reduces fluid retention, and lowers blood pressure. It also provides kidney-protective benefits by reducing pressure inside the kidney's filtering units.

commonSideEffects.advice: This is a well-known side effect of ACE inhibitors. If it becomes intolerable, your doctor may switch you to an ARB (like losartan) which rarely causes cough.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common, especially with the first dose or dose increases
commonSideEffects.advice: Take the first dose at bedtime. Stand up slowly. Stay well hydrated.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common in the first few weeks
commonSideEffects.advice: Usually settles as your body adjusts. A mild painkiller can help.
This usually improves within a few weeks. Avoid driving if you feel unusually tired.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat (angioedema)
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a medical emergency. Stop taking lisinopril and seek emergency medical help immediately, even if swelling seems mild — it can worsen rapidly.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of high potassium: muscle weakness, slow or irregular heartbeat, tingling or numbness
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor immediately. You may need blood tests to check your potassium level.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium
avoidanceWarnings.reason: Lisinopril raises potassium levels. Adding extra potassium can cause dangerously high levels that affect your heart.

storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-30 degrees Celsius. Protect from moisture and light. Keep in the original container.

description: Simvastatin is a statin medication that lowers cholesterol levels to reduce your risk of heart attack and stroke. It is commonly prescribed alongside blood pressure medications for people with diabetes or hypertension.
howItWorks: Simvastatin blocks an enzyme called HMG-CoA reductase in your liver, which is responsible for making cholesterol. With less cholesterol being produced, your liver pulls more LDL (bad) cholesterol out of your blood to meet its needs. This lowers LDL cholesterol and triglycerides while modestly raising HDL (good) cholesterol. Simvastatin works best when taken in the evening, as your liver produces the most cholesterol at night.

commonSideEffects.advice: Mild muscle aches are usually harmless and often settle. Stay active and hydrated. Tell your doctor if pain is persistent or gets worse.
Usually improves within the first few weeks.
Take with your evening meal. Symptoms usually settle.
Increase fibre and water intake. Gentle exercise can also help.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially with fever or dark brown urine (rhabdomyolysis)
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking simvastatin and seek emergency medical attention immediately. This is rare but can cause kidney damage.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin or eyes, dark urine, unusual tiredness, persistent nausea
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor immediately for liver function tests.

storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-30 degrees Celsius. Keep in the original container, tightly closed. Protect from moisture.

description: Metoprolol is a beta-blocker used to treat high blood pressure, chest pain (angina), and heart failure. It slows your heart rate and reduces the force of each heartbeat, lowering the demand on your heart.
howItWorks: Metoprolol blocks beta-1 receptors on your heart and blood vessels. These receptors normally respond to adrenaline and similar stress hormones by making your heart beat faster and harder. By blocking them, metoprolol slows your heart rate, lowers your blood pressure, and reduces the oxygen your heart needs. This makes it particularly useful after a heart attack or in heart failure.

commonSideEffects.advice: This usually improves over 1-2 weeks. Take your dose at bedtime if daytime tiredness is a problem.
Wear warm gloves and socks. This is caused by reduced blood flow to extremities and is usually mild.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common when starting or increasing dose
commonSideEffects.advice: Stand up slowly. Avoid sudden position changes.
A slower resting heart rate (50-60 beats per minute) is normal on metoprolol. Contact your doctor if it drops below 50 or you feel faint.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Very slow heartbeat (below 45 bpm), severe dizziness, or fainting
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek medical attention. Your dose may need to be reduced.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Worsening shortness of breath or sudden weight gain (signs of worsening heart failure)

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Verapamil or diltiazem (certain calcium channel blockers)
avoidanceWarnings.reason: Combining these with metoprolol can cause your heart rate to drop dangerously low. Only use together under close medical supervision.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if your resting heart rate drops below 50 beats per minute, if you experience worsening shortness of breath, or if you gain weight suddenly. Never stop taking metoprolol without talking to your doctor first.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-25 degrees Celsius. Protect from moisture and light. Keep in the original packaging.

description: Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that reduces stomach acid production. It is used to treat acid reflux, stomach ulcers, and to protect the stomach from damage caused by NSAIDs or aspirin, which are commonly used alongside blood pressure and diabetes medications.
howItWorks: Omeprazole irreversibly blocks the proton pumps (tiny acid-producing units) in the lining of your stomach. These pumps normally produce hydrochloric acid to help digest food. By shutting them down, omeprazole reduces stomach acid by up to 90%. New pumps are constantly being made, which is why you need to take it daily. It works best when taken 30 minutes before breakfast.

commonSideEffects.advice: Usually mild and improves within a few days.
These are usually mild and temporary. Take with a glass of water before meals.
Reduced stomach acid can change digestion patterns. This usually settles.
Increase fibre and water intake.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of low magnesium (with long-term use): muscle spasms, irregular heartbeat, tremors, seizures
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor. You may need a blood test to check magnesium levels, especially if you have been taking omeprazole for more than a year.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe diarrhoea with stomach cramps and fever (possible C. difficile infection)
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor urgently. Do not take anti-diarrhoea medicines without medical advice.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Omeprazole can reduce the effectiveness of clopidogrel, a blood thinner. If you need both, your doctor may switch to a different acid reducer.

description: Gliclazide is a sulfonylurea medication used to treat type 2 diabetes. It stimulates your pancreas to release more insulin and also improves how your body uses insulin, helping to control blood sugar levels throughout the day.
howItWorks: Gliclazide binds to receptors on insulin-producing cells in your pancreas, stimulating them to release insulin. The modified-release form provides steady blood sugar control over 24 hours.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent stomach pain
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor immediately.

description: Pioglitazone is a thiazolidinedione medication used to treat type 2 diabetes. It makes your body's cells more sensitive to insulin, allowing them to absorb sugar from your blood more effectively. It is often used when metformin alone is not enough.
howItWorks: Pioglitazone activates a receptor called PPAR-gamma inside your fat, muscle, and liver cells. When activated, these cells become more responsive to insulin, allowing more sugar to move from your blood into your cells. It also reduces the amount of fat stored in your liver and decreases certain inflammatory signals. The full effect takes 2-3 months to develop.

commonSideEffects.advice: Some weight gain is expected, partly due to fluid retention and partly due to increased fat storage under the skin. Maintain a healthy diet and exercise regularly.

commonSideEffects.effect: Fluid retention and swelling in ankles or feet
commonSideEffects.advice: Elevate your feet. Tell your doctor if swelling is significant, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
Usually improves within a few days.
Mild cold-like symptoms may occur. See your doctor if they persist.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of heart failure: rapid weight gain, worsening shortness of breath, swelling in legs or feet, difficulty lying flat
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking pioglitazone and seek medical help immediately. Pioglitazone can cause or worsen heart failure in some people.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, unusual tiredness, stomach pain
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor immediately for liver function tests.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Pioglitazone causes fluid retention, which can trigger or worsen heart failure. Tell your doctor immediately if you have any history of heart problems.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek urgent help if you experience sudden weight gain, increasing shortness of breath, or significant swelling in your legs. Contact your doctor if you notice blood in your urine, visual changes, or any bone pain (pioglitazone may affect bone density with long-term use).
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-30 degrees Celsius. Keep in the original packaging, protected from moisture and humidity.

description: Furosemide is a powerful loop diuretic (water pill) used to reduce fluid build-up in conditions like heart failure, kidney disease, and severe hypertension. It works faster and more strongly than thiazide diuretics like hydrochlorothiazide.
howItWorks: Furosemide works in a part of the kidney called the loop of Henle, where it blocks the reabsorption of sodium, chloride, and potassium. This causes your kidneys to pass out much more water and salt in your urine, rapidly reducing fluid overload. The effect starts within 30-60 minutes of taking a tablet and lasts about 6 hours. This makes it very effective for relieving fluid build-up around the lungs or in the legs.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take in the morning (or morning and midday if twice daily) to avoid night-time bathroom trips.
Stand up slowly. Drink adequate fluids, but follow your doctor's advice on fluid limits if you have heart failure.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common, due to loss of potassium and magnesium
commonSideEffects.advice: Eat potassium-rich foods (bananas, oranges, potatoes). Your doctor may prescribe potassium supplements.
Drink water as needed, but follow any fluid restrictions your doctor has set.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe dehydration: extreme thirst, very dry mouth, confusion, dark concentrated urine, rapid heartbeat
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking furosemide and seek medical attention immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe electrolyte imbalance: irregular heartbeat, severe muscle weakness or cramps, confusion, seizures
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help. You need urgent blood tests to check your electrolyte levels.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: These painkillers can significantly reduce the effectiveness of furosemide and increase the risk of kidney damage.
Both furosemide and aminoglycosides can damage hearing. Combined use significantly increases this risk.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek urgent medical help if you experience irregular heartbeat, severe muscle cramps, confusion, or difficulty hearing. Contact your doctor if you stop passing urine, have extreme thirst, or feel severely dizzy. Weigh yourself daily — sudden weight gain of more than 1 kg in a day may mean fluid is building up again.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-25 degrees Celsius. Protect from light (furosemide is light-sensitive). Keep in the original container, tightly closed.

description: The HbA1c test (also called glycated haemoglobin or A1c) is a blood test that measures your average blood sugar level over the past 2-3 months. It is the most important routine test for monitoring diabetes control.
howItWorks: When sugar is in your blood, some of it attaches to haemoglobin — the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. The HbA1c test measures the percentage of haemoglobin that has sugar attached. Because red blood cells live for about 3 months, the test reflects your average blood sugar over that period. A higher HbA1c means more sugar has been attaching to your blood cells, indicating higher average blood sugar levels.

commonSideEffects.effect: Slight discomfort from the blood draw
commonSideEffects.advice: This is a simple blood test. Any pain from the needle is brief. Press on the site for a few minutes afterwards to prevent bruising.

seriousSideEffects.effect: There are no side effects from the test itself
seriousSideEffects.action: The HbA1c is a safe blood test with no medical risks beyond a minor blood draw.

whenToSeekHelp: Discuss your results with your doctor. Target ranges are typically: below 7% (53 mmol/mol) for most people with diabetes, though your doctor may set a different target based on your age, health, and risk of low blood sugar. An HbA1c above 8% usually means your treatment plan needs adjustment.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — this is a laboratory test, not a medication. Your doctor or lab will handle the blood sample.

description: Metformin ni dawa inayotumiwa sana kwa ugonjwa wa kisukari aina ya 2. Inapunguza kiasi cha sukari ambacho ini yako inazalisha na kusaidia mwili wako kutumia insulini vizuri zaidi.
howItWorks: Metformin inafanya kazi kwa njia tatu: inapunguza kiasi cha sukari inayozalishwa na ini yako, inapunguza kasi ya kunyonya sukari kutoka kwenye utumbo wako, na inasaidia seli za misuli yako kutumia insulini vizuri zaidi. Haifanyi mwili wako kuzalisha insulini zaidi, ndiyo sababu mara chache husababisha sukari ya damu kushuka sana peke yake.

commonSideEffects.advice: Tumia dawa pamoja na chakula. Dalili hizi huisha mwili unapoizoea.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Kawaida wakati wa kuanza au kuongeza dozi
commonSideEffects.advice: Anza na dozi ndogo na uongeze taratibu. Kunywa maji mengi.
Hii si hatari na huisha yenyewe.
Kula milo midogo mara kwa mara hata kama huna hamu ya kula.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Lactic acidosis (nadra sana): maumivu ya misuli yasiyo ya kawaida, ugumu wa kupumua, maumivu ya tumbo, kuhisi baridi, kizunguzungu
seriousSideEffects.action: Acha kutumia metformin na nenda hospitali mara moja. Hii ni nadra lakini ni hatari.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Mzio mkubwa: upele, kuvimba, ugumu wa kupumua
seriousSideEffects.action: Tafuta msaada wa dharura wa matibabu mara moja.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Kunywa pombe wakati unatumia metformin kunaongeza hatari ya lactic acidosis na kunaweza kusababisha sukari ya damu kushuka sana.
Mkarela inaweza kupunguza sukari ya damu yenyewe. Kuchanganya na metformin kunaweza kusababisha sukari ya damu kushuka sana.

whenToSeekHelp: Wasiliana na daktari wako ukipata kutapika kwa muda mrefu, maumivu makubwa ya tumbo, uchovu usio wa kawaida, au misuli kukakamaa. Ukihisi baridi sana, kizunguzungu, au ugumu wa kupumua, nenda chumba cha dharura mara moja.
storageInstructions: Hifadhi kwa joto la kawaida kati ya nyuzi joto 15-25. Weka kwenye chombo cha asili na kifuniko kimefungwa vizuri. Linda kutokana na unyevu na mwanga. Usihifadhi bafuni.

description: Salbutamol is a fast-acting bronchodilator (reliever inhaler) used to quickly open your airways during an asthma attack or when you feel wheezy or short of breath.
howItWorks: Salbutamol relaxes the muscles around your airways within minutes. When you inhale it, the medicine goes directly to your lungs and makes the tight, narrowed airways open wider so air can flow freely. Relief usually starts within 5 minutes and lasts 4-6 hours.

commonSideEffects.advice: This usually settles after a few minutes and improves with regular use.
Sit quietly for a few minutes after using your inhaler. This is usually harmless.
Drink water and rest. Take a mild painkiller if needed.
Ensure you are drinking enough water and eating potassium-rich foods like bananas.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Chest pain or very fast irregular heartbeat
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop using and seek emergency help immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No relief from usual dose or needing it more than 3 times a week
seriousSideEffects.action: See your doctor — your asthma may not be well controlled and your treatment may need adjusting.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Can increase heart rate and tremor when combined with salbutamol.
Beta-blockers can block the effect of salbutamol and may worsen asthma.

whenToSeekHelp: If you need your reliever more than 3 times a week, your asthma is not well controlled. If salbutamol does not relieve your symptoms within 10 minutes, use it again and call for emergency help if still no relief.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C. Do not puncture or expose the canister to heat or flame. Keep the cap on when not in use. Check the dose counter and get a new inhaler before it runs out.

description: Beclomethasone is a steroid preventer inhaler that reduces inflammation in your airways over time, making asthma attacks less likely when used every day.
howItWorks: Beclomethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces swelling, mucus, and irritation inside your airways. Unlike a reliever inhaler, it does not work immediately — it takes 1-2 weeks of regular daily use to reach its full effect. It prevents attacks rather than treating them.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common if not rinsing after use
commonSideEffects.advice: Always rinse your mouth with water and spit it out after each use.
Rinsing after use helps. It improves if you rest your voice.
Gargle with warm salt water. Rinsing after use helps prevent this.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of adrenal suppression (extreme tiredness, weight loss, dizziness) after long-term high-dose use
seriousSideEffects.action: Do not stop suddenly — see your doctor to adjust your dose gradually.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction: swelling of face, tongue, or throat
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help immediately.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Your body depends on the steroid. Stopping abruptly can cause adrenal crisis. Always taper under doctor guidance.
Steroid inhalers can worsen untreated lung infections. Tell your doctor if you have TB or a chest infection.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop persistent white patches in your mouth, if your asthma symptoms worsen despite regular use, or if you get frequent chest infections.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C away from direct sunlight. Do not freeze. Keep the mouthpiece cap on when not in use. Replace as directed by the dose counter.

description: Montelukast is a leukotriene blocker taken as a daily tablet to prevent asthma symptoms and reduce the need for reliever inhalers.
howItWorks: Montelukast blocks chemicals called leukotrienes that cause airway inflammation, swelling, and mucus production. By blocking these, it helps keep airways open and reduces sensitivity to asthma triggers. It is taken once daily, usually in the evening.

commonSideEffects.advice: Usually mild and improves over time. Take a mild painkiller if needed.
Take with food if this occurs.
Taking it in the evening can help, as you sleep through the drowsiness.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Mood changes, depression, unusual thoughts, or agitation
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking montelukast and contact your doctor immediately. These are rare but important to report.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical help immediately.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: These medicines can reduce montelukast levels in your blood, making it less effective.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you notice mood changes, anxiety, depression, or sleep disturbances. Also seek help if your asthma symptoms do not improve after 2 weeks of regular use.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C. Protect from moisture and light. Keep in the original packaging until ready to take.

description: Tamoxifen is a hormone therapy used to treat and prevent breast cancer. It blocks the effects of oestrogen on breast tissue, slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells that depend on this hormone.
howItWorks: Tamoxifen is a selective oestrogen receptor modulator (SERM). It binds to oestrogen receptors on breast cancer cells, blocking the hormone oestrogen from attaching. Without oestrogen stimulation, the cancer cells stop growing and dividing. It is taken daily for 5-10 years.

commonSideEffects.advice: Wear light layers, keep cool drinks nearby. These usually lessen over the first few months.
Take with food. Symptoms usually improve as your body adjusts.
Discuss with your doctor. Do not use oestrogen-containing products.
Rest when needed. Light exercise can help manage tiredness.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Unusual vaginal bleeding
seriousSideEffects.action: See your doctor promptly — this needs investigation.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Leg swelling, pain, or shortness of breath (possible blood clot)
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical attention immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Vision changes or eye pain
seriousSideEffects.action: See an eye doctor — tamoxifen can rarely affect the eyes.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: These directly oppose the action of tamoxifen and can reduce its effectiveness.
These antidepressants can reduce your body's ability to convert tamoxifen into its active form, making it less effective.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you have unusual vaginal bleeding, leg pain or swelling, persistent cough, vision changes, or severe headaches.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 20-25°C. Protect from light. Keep out of reach of children and away from heat.

description: Capecitabine is an oral chemotherapy medicine used to treat breast, stomach, and bowel cancers. It is converted into the active drug 5-fluorouracil inside cancer cells.
howItWorks: Capecitabine is a prodrug that your body converts into 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), mostly within tumour cells. 5-FU stops cancer cells from making DNA and RNA, which they need to grow and divide. This targeted activation means more of the drug works where it is needed.

commonSideEffects.advice: Drink plenty of fluids. Tell your doctor if you have more than 4 watery stools a day.
Take anti-nausea medicine as prescribed. Eat small, frequent meals.

commonSideEffects.effect: Hand-foot syndrome (red, swollen, painful palms and soles)
commonSideEffects.advice: Moisturise hands and feet. Avoid hot water. Tell your doctor early — dose may need adjusting.
Rest when needed. Plan activities for when you have more energy.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe diarrhoea (more than 4 times daily) or vomiting that won't stop
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking capecitabine and contact your doctor or go to hospital immediately. You may need IV fluids.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Chest pain or irregular heartbeat
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help immediately — capecitabine can affect the heart.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of infection: fever above 38°C, chills
seriousSideEffects.action: Go to hospital immediately — chemotherapy can lower your immune system.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Capecitabine can greatly increase the blood-thinning effect, causing dangerous bleeding. Your doctor must monitor closely.
Capecitabine can increase phenytoin levels to dangerous amounts.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor immediately if you develop a fever, severe diarrhoea, vomiting you cannot control, hand-foot syndrome, chest pain, or mouth sores so bad you cannot eat or drink.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C. Keep in the original packaging. Take within 30 minutes after meals with water. Return unused tablets to your pharmacy — do not dispose of at home.

description: Imatinib is a targeted cancer therapy used mainly for chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) and some gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST). It works by blocking a specific protein that drives cancer cell growth.
howItWorks: Imatinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor. It specifically blocks the BCR-ABL protein in CML and the KIT protein in GIST. By blocking these proteins, it stops cancer cells from receiving growth signals, causing them to die while leaving most normal cells unharmed.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with a large glass of water during a meal to reduce stomach upset.
Stay hydrated. Gentle stretching and calcium/magnesium supplements may help — ask your doctor.

commonSideEffects.effect: Swelling around eyes, ankles, or feet
commonSideEffects.advice: This is usually mild. Reduce salt intake. Tell your doctor if it worsens.
Use fragrance-free moisturiser. Tell your doctor if it spreads or becomes severe.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe fluid retention: sudden weight gain, difficulty breathing, swollen abdomen
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek urgent medical attention — may indicate serious fluid build-up.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe nausea
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking imatinib and see your doctor immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe bleeding or unusual bruising
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical help.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Reduces imatinib blood levels, making it less effective against cancer.
Both imatinib and paracetamol are processed by the liver. Using both can increase liver strain.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop sudden weight gain, difficulty breathing, yellowing of skin or eyes, severe rash, persistent fever, or unusual bleeding.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture. Keep in original packaging. Take at the same time each day with food and a full glass of water.

description: Erythropoietin (EPO) is an injection used to treat anaemia caused by chronic kidney disease. It stimulates your bone marrow to produce more red blood cells, reducing tiredness and the need for blood transfusions.
howItWorks: Healthy kidneys produce a hormone called erythropoietin that tells your bone marrow to make red blood cells. When kidneys are damaged, they produce less of this hormone, causing anaemia. The injection replaces the missing hormone, boosting red blood cell production over several weeks.

commonSideEffects.advice: Rotate injection sites. Apply a cold cloth after injection.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common, especially when haemoglobin is rising
commonSideEffects.advice: Take a mild painkiller. Tell your doctor if headaches are severe.
Usually mild and temporary. Gentle movement can help.
Usually improves with continued use.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Sudden severe headache, confusion, or seizures (possible high blood pressure crisis)
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of blood clot: leg pain/swelling, chest pain, sudden shortness of breath
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical attention immediately.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Iron-depleting foods or supplements without guidance
avoidanceWarnings.reason: EPO needs iron to make red blood cells. Your doctor will check iron levels and prescribe supplements if needed.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop severe headaches, leg swelling, chest pain, or if you feel more tired despite treatment. Regular blood tests are essential to monitor your response.
storageInstructions: Store in a refrigerator at 2-8°C. Do not freeze. Protect from light. Take out 30 minutes before injecting to reach room temperature. Do not shake.

description: Calcium carbonate is used in kidney disease as a phosphate binder to control high phosphate levels, and as a calcium supplement to protect bones weakened by kidney disease.
howItWorks: In kidney disease, the kidneys cannot remove phosphate properly, leading to dangerous build-up. Calcium carbonate binds to phosphate in food during digestion, preventing it from being absorbed into your blood. It must be taken with meals to work as a phosphate binder.

commonSideEffects.advice: Drink more water and eat high-fibre foods. Ask your doctor about stool softeners if needed.
Take with meals as directed. Symptoms usually improve over time.
Take with food. Chewable tablets may be easier on the stomach.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of high calcium: excessive thirst, frequent urination, confusion, muscle weakness
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor promptly — your calcium levels may need checking.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Kidney stones: severe flank pain, blood in urine
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek medical attention.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Take iron at least 2 hours apart from calcium — calcium reduces iron absorption.
Take antibiotics at least 2 hours before or after calcium to avoid reduced absorption.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop severe constipation, muscle cramps, confusion, or signs of kidney stones.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C. Keep dry. Close the container tightly after use.

description: Digoxin is a heart medicine used to treat heart failure and irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation). It helps your heart beat more strongly and at a more regular rhythm.
howItWorks: Digoxin works by increasing the force of each heartbeat, helping a weak heart pump blood more effectively. It also slows electrical signals through the heart, which helps control a fast or irregular heart rhythm. It has a very narrow safety range — the dose must be carefully monitored.

commonSideEffects.advice: Tell your doctor — this can be an early sign the dose is too high.
Stand up slowly. Tell your doctor if it persists.
Rest when needed. Report persistent tiredness to your doctor.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Visual disturbances: blurred vision, seeing yellow/green halos
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking digoxin and see your doctor immediately — this may indicate toxic levels.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Very slow heartbeat (below 60 bpm), dizziness, or fainting
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe nausea, vomiting, confusion
seriousSideEffects.action: Go to hospital — possible digoxin toxicity.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Reduces digoxin levels in the blood, making it less effective.
Can reduce digoxin absorption. Take 2 hours apart.
Low potassium increases the risk of digoxin toxicity. Eat potassium-rich foods like bananas and oranges.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you feel unusually tired, nauseous, see visual changes, or notice your heart beating very slowly or irregularly. Regular blood tests are needed to check digoxin levels.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-25°C. Protect from light. Take at the same time every day. Keep all follow-up blood test appointments.

description: Warfarin is a blood-thinning medicine (anticoagulant) used to prevent and treat blood clots. It is prescribed after heart valve replacement, for atrial fibrillation, deep vein thrombosis, or stroke prevention.
howItWorks: Warfarin blocks vitamin K, which your liver needs to make clotting factors. With less clotting factor, your blood takes longer to clot, reducing the chance of dangerous clots forming in your heart, lungs, or blood vessels. It requires regular blood tests (INR) to ensure the dose is correct.

commonSideEffects.advice: Be careful to avoid bumps and cuts. Apply pressure to any cuts for longer than usual.
Use a soft toothbrush. Tell your doctor if bleeding is heavy.
Track your periods and tell your doctor if they become much heavier.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Unusual or heavy bleeding: blood in urine or stool, nosebleeds that won't stop, coughing blood
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical help immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe headache or sudden confusion (possible brain bleed)
seriousSideEffects.action: Go to hospital immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Black tarry stools (possible internal bleeding)
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical attention.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Green leafy vegetables in inconsistent amounts
avoidanceWarnings.reason: These are high in vitamin K. Eat a consistent amount daily — sudden changes can make warfarin less effective or too strong.
Heavy alcohol use increases bleeding risk and affects how your liver processes warfarin.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Aspirin or ibuprofen without doctor approval
avoidanceWarnings.reason: These increase bleeding risk significantly when combined with warfarin.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek immediate help for blood in urine or stool, heavy nosebleeds, severe headache, unusual bruising, or any signs of heavy bleeding. Never skip INR blood tests.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature between 15-30°C. Protect from light and moisture. Take at the same time every day. Carry a card or wear a bracelet saying you take warfarin.

description: Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet medicine that prevents blood clots. It is used after a heart attack, stroke, or in people with peripheral arterial disease to reduce the risk of further events.
howItWorks: Clopidogrel stops platelets (tiny blood cells) from sticking together and forming clots. It irreversibly blocks a receptor called P2Y12 on the surface of platelets. Once a platelet is blocked, it cannot form clots for its entire 7-10 day lifespan.

commonSideEffects.advice: Be careful to avoid injuries. This is a sign the medicine is working.
Pinch your nose for 10 minutes. Use a humidifier if air is dry.
Take with food. Tell your doctor if symptoms persist.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Blood in stool, urine, or vomit
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical help immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe headache, confusion, or weakness on one side (possible stroke)
seriousSideEffects.action: Call emergency services immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Tiny red spots under the skin, unusual paleness, fever (possible TTP — a rare blood condition)
seriousSideEffects.action: Go to hospital immediately — this is rare but life-threatening.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: These stomach medicines can reduce clopidogrel's effectiveness. Ask your doctor for alternatives like pantoprazole.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Aspirin (unless prescribed together by your doctor)
avoidanceWarnings.reason: Both thin the blood. Using together increases bleeding risk — only combine if your doctor specifically says to.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek emergency help for any unusual bleeding, blood in stool or urine, severe headache, or signs of stroke. Do not stop taking clopidogrel without talking to your doctor first.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C. Protect from moisture. Take at the same time each day. Tell any doctor or dentist you see that you take clopidogrel, especially before surgery.

description: Isosorbide mononitrate is a nitrate medicine used to prevent angina (chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart). It widens blood vessels to improve blood supply to the heart.
howItWorks: Isosorbide mononitrate releases nitric oxide, which relaxes and widens blood vessels. This reduces the workload on the heart and improves blood flow to the heart muscle. It prevents angina attacks but does not stop one that has already started — use GTN spray for that.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take a mild painkiller. Headaches usually lessen after the first 1-2 weeks as your body adjusts.
Stand up slowly. Avoid alcohol, which worsens this effect.
This is harmless and usually brief.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Fainting or very low blood pressure
seriousSideEffects.action: Lie down with legs raised. If it happens repeatedly, see your doctor — the dose may need adjusting.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe headache that doesn't respond to painkillers
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor — the dose may need adjusting.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Sildenafil (Viagra) or similar erectile dysfunction medicines
avoidanceWarnings.reason: Combining these with nitrates can cause a dangerous, life-threatening drop in blood pressure.
Alcohol widens blood vessels further, increasing dizziness and the risk of fainting.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if headaches are severe and persistent, if you faint, or if your angina attacks become more frequent despite taking this medicine.
storageInstructions: Store below 25°C in a dry place. Protect from light. Take as prescribed — do not skip doses or double up.

description: Hydroxyurea is the main disease-modifying medicine for sickle cell disease. It reduces the frequency and severity of pain crises, acute chest syndrome, and the need for blood transfusions.
howItWorks: Hydroxyurea increases production of foetal haemoglobin (HbF) in red blood cells. Foetal haemoglobin prevents the sickle haemoglobin from forming the rigid shapes that cause cells to stick and block blood vessels. It also reduces inflammation and improves blood flow.

commonSideEffects.effect: Reduced blood counts (lower white cells, platelets)
commonSideEffects.frequency: Common — monitored by regular blood tests
commonSideEffects.advice: Attend all blood test appointments. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on results.
Take with food or in the evening. Symptoms usually improve over time.
Harmless but may be noticeable. Use sunscreen on exposed skin.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of low blood counts: fever, unusual bleeding or bruising, extreme tiredness
seriousSideEffects.action: See your doctor urgently — your blood counts may be too low and the dose may need pausing.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Mouth sores or difficulty swallowing
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor — may indicate the dose needs adjusting.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Hydroxyurea suppresses the immune system. Live vaccines may cause infection.
Hydroxyurea can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable contraception and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop a fever, unusual bleeding or bruising, severe tiredness, or mouth sores. Never miss blood test appointments while on this medicine.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C. Keep capsules dry. Handle with care — wash hands after touching capsules. Keep away from children.

description: Folic acid is a B vitamin supplement essential for sickle cell patients. It supports the rapid production of new red blood cells needed to replace the sickle cells that break down prematurely.
howItWorks: Red blood cells in sickle cell disease have a much shorter lifespan (10-20 days vs 120 days normal). Your bone marrow works overtime to replace them and needs extra folic acid to make DNA for new cells. Without enough folic acid, you develop folate-deficiency anaemia on top of sickle cell anaemia.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food if this occurs.
This is usually temporary and resolves on its own.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking and see your doctor. True folic acid allergy is very rare.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: If you also take methotrexate, your doctor will tell you specific days to take folic acid — taking it at the wrong time reduces methotrexate's effect.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you feel increasingly tired despite taking folic acid, develop a rash, or notice yellowing of your skin or eyes.
storageInstructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from light and moisture. Keep in the original container.

description: TLD is a single-tablet combination of three antiretroviral medicines (tenofovir, lamivudine, and dolutegravir) taken once daily to treat HIV. It is the recommended first-line treatment in Kenya.
howItWorks: The three medicines attack HIV at different stages of its life cycle. Tenofovir and lamivudine block reverse transcriptase (the enzyme HIV uses to copy its genetic material), while dolutegravir blocks integrase (the enzyme HIV uses to insert its DNA into your cells). Together, they prevent the virus from multiplying.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common in the first few weeks
commonSideEffects.advice: Usually improves within 2-4 weeks. Take a mild painkiller if needed.
Take with food. Symptoms usually settle within 2 weeks.
Taking the tablet in the morning instead of evening may help.
Maintain a balanced diet and regular exercise. Discuss with your doctor if significant.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of kidney problems: reduced urine, swelling in legs, persistent nausea
seriousSideEffects.action: See your doctor promptly — tenofovir can affect kidneys in some people.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of lactic acidosis: unusual muscle pain, stomach pain, difficulty breathing, feeling cold
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency medical help immediately. This is rare but serious.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Take dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after these — they reduce dolutegravir absorption.
Reduces dolutegravir levels significantly. Your doctor may need to adjust your ARV regimen.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop a rash, persistent stomach pain, muscle aches, reduced urination, or yellowing of eyes. Never stop ARVs without talking to your doctor — this can cause drug resistance.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture. Take at the same time every day with or without food. Do not split or crush the tablet.

description: Nevirapine is an antiretroviral medicine (NNRTI) used as part of combination therapy to treat HIV. In Kenya, it is used as an alternative regimen when TLD is not suitable.
howItWorks: Nevirapine blocks reverse transcriptase, the enzyme HIV uses to copy its genetic material. By attaching directly to this enzyme, it prevents the virus from making new copies of itself. It is always used with other ARVs — never alone.

commonSideEffects.advice: Start with a lower dose for 2 weeks to reduce rash risk. Tell your doctor about any rash immediately.
Usually mild and improves over time.
Take with food. Usually settles after the first few weeks.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe rash with blisters, mouth sores, or fever (Stevens-Johnson syndrome)
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop nevirapine immediately and go to hospital. This is a medical emergency.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Yellowing of eyes or skin, dark urine, severe nausea (liver damage)
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking and seek medical help immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Fever combined with rash
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop nevirapine and see your doctor urgently — this combination is a danger sign.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Reduces nevirapine levels in the blood, risking HIV drug resistance.

description: Carbamazepine is one of the most commonly used anti-seizure medicines in Kenya. It controls partial and generalised tonic-clonic seizures and is also used for trigeminal neuralgia (severe face pain).

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common when starting or increasing dose
commonSideEffects.advice: Your body adjusts over 1-2 weeks. Avoid driving until you know how it affects you.
Stand up slowly. Report to your doctor if persistent — the dose may need adjusting.

seriousSideEffects.action: See your doctor urgently for a blood test.

seriousSideEffects.action: See your doctor immediately.

description: Sodium valproate is a broad-spectrum anti-seizure medicine effective against many types of epilepsy. It is particularly good for generalised seizures, absence seizures, and myoclonic jerks.
howItWorks: Sodium valproate increases levels of GABA, a calming chemical in the brain that prevents excessive electrical activity. It also blocks sodium and calcium channels in neurons. This combination makes it effective against a wide range of seizure types.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with or after food. Enteric-coated tablets cause less stomach upset.
Maintain a balanced diet and regular exercise. Discuss with your doctor if significant.

seriousSideEffects.action: See your doctor for a blood test.

description: Phenytoin is an anti-seizure medicine used to control partial seizures and generalised tonic-clonic (grand mal) seizures. It has been used for decades and is widely available in Kenya.
howItWorks: Phenytoin stabilises nerve cell membranes by blocking sodium channels, preventing the repetitive firing of neurons that causes seizures. It has a narrow therapeutic range, meaning blood levels must be carefully monitored to stay effective without causing toxicity.

commonSideEffects.advice: Brush teeth carefully twice daily and floss. See a dentist regularly.

seriousSideEffects.action: See your doctor for a blood test — phenytoin can rarely affect blood counts.

Phenytoin reduces their effectiveness. Use additional contraception methods.
Phenytoin interacts with many drugs. Always tell any doctor or pharmacist that you take phenytoin.

description: Phenobarbital is one of the oldest and most affordable anti-seizure medicines. It remains widely used in Kenya and other African countries due to its effectiveness and low cost.
howItWorks: Phenobarbital enhances the effect of GABA, the brain's main calming neurotransmitter. It binds to GABA-A receptors and makes them respond more strongly, reducing the excessive electrical activity that causes seizures.

commonSideEffects.advice: Usually improves over 1-2 weeks as your body adjusts. Avoid driving or operating machinery.
Schedule important tasks for when you feel most alert.

seriousSideEffects.action: Stop phenobarbital and go to hospital immediately.

description: Tiotropium is a long-acting bronchodilator inhaler used as daily maintenance treatment for COPD. It keeps airways open for 24 hours, making breathing easier throughout the day.
howItWorks: Tiotropium blocks acetylcholine receptors (muscarinic receptors) in the airways. By blocking these, it prevents the muscles around your airways from tightening, keeping them relaxed and open. Unlike a reliever, it works continuously for 24 hours with once-daily use.

commonSideEffects.advice: Sip water regularly. Sugar-free gum or sweets can help stimulate saliva.
Rinse your mouth with water after inhaling.
Drink more fluids and eat high-fibre foods.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if your breathing worsens, you have difficulty urinating, or you develop eye pain after accidental eye exposure.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture. Do not swallow the capsules — they are for the inhaler device only. Replace the inhaler as directed.

description: Ipratropium is a short-acting bronchodilator inhaler used to relieve breathlessness in COPD and severe asthma. It works within 15 minutes and lasts 4-6 hours.
howItWorks: Like tiotropium, ipratropium blocks acetylcholine from tightening the muscles around your airways. It acts faster but for a shorter time. It is often used as a rescue inhaler for COPD or combined with salbutamol in a nebuliser during acute episodes.

commonSideEffects.advice: Rinse mouth after use. Sip water regularly.
Rinse mouth with water after use. This is harmless.

description: Prednisolone is a corticosteroid tablet used for short courses during asthma or COPD flare-ups, and for longer-term treatment of inflammatory conditions like arthritis and autoimmune diseases.
howItWorks: Prednisolone powerfully reduces inflammation by suppressing the immune system's inflammatory response. It blocks the production of chemicals that cause swelling, redness, and pain. For asthma/COPD flares, short courses (5-7 days) rapidly reduce airway inflammation.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common with courses longer than 2 weeks

Take the dose in the morning. Avoid caffeine in the afternoon.

description: Diclofenac is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) widely used in Kenya for arthritis pain, inflammation, and swelling. It is available as tablets, gel, and injection.
howItWorks: Diclofenac blocks enzymes called COX-1 and COX-2 that produce prostaglandins — chemicals that cause pain, inflammation, and swelling. By reducing prostaglandins, it relieves joint pain and stiffness, allowing better movement.

description: Methotrexate is a disease-modifying medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis and some cancers. For arthritis, it is taken once weekly (not daily) at low doses to slow joint damage and reduce inflammation.
howItWorks: At low doses for arthritis, methotrexate reduces the overactive immune response that attacks your joints. It inhibits an enzyme involved in cell growth, which dampens the inflammatory cells causing joint damage. Benefits take 6-12 weeks to become noticeable.

description: Ibuprofen is a widely available NSAID used for pain relief, inflammation, and fever. It is commonly used for arthritis, headaches, menstrual pain, and general aches.
howItWorks: Ibuprofen blocks COX enzymes that produce prostaglandins — chemicals that cause pain, fever, and inflammation. It starts working within 30-60 minutes and its effects last 4-6 hours.

description: Celecoxib is a COX-2 selective NSAID used for arthritis pain and inflammation. It is gentler on the stomach than traditional NSAIDs like diclofenac or ibuprofen.

description: Fluoxetine is an SSRI antidepressant used to treat depression, anxiety, OCD, and panic disorder. It is one of the most prescribed mental health medicines in Kenya.
howItWorks: Fluoxetine increases the amount of serotonin available in your brain. Serotonin is a chemical messenger that regulates mood, sleep, and anxiety. By blocking its reabsorption, more serotonin stays active between nerve cells. Full benefits take 4-6 weeks.

description: Amitriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant used at higher doses for depression and at lower doses for chronic pain conditions, migraines, and nerve pain.
howItWorks: Amitriptyline increases levels of serotonin and noradrenaline in the brain by blocking their reabsorption. It also blocks certain pain signals in the nervous system, which is why lower doses help with chronic pain even without depression.

description: Haloperidol is an antipsychotic medicine used to treat schizophrenia, acute psychosis, severe agitation, and Tourette syndrome. It helps control hallucinations, delusions, and disordered thinking.
howItWorks: Haloperidol blocks dopamine D2 receptors in the brain. Excess dopamine activity is linked to psychotic symptoms. By reducing this overactivity, haloperidol reduces hallucinations, paranoia, and agitation, helping restore clearer thinking.

description: Diazepam is a benzodiazepine used for short-term treatment of severe anxiety, muscle spasms, seizure emergencies, and alcohol withdrawal. It is also used rectally to stop prolonged seizures in epilepsy.
howItWorks: Diazepam enhances the effect of GABA, the brain's main calming chemical. It binds to GABA-A receptors and amplifies their calming signal, rapidly reducing anxiety, muscle tension, and seizure activity. Effects are felt within 15-30 minutes.

commonSideEffects.advice: Do not drive or operate machinery. Take at bedtime if prescribed for sleep.
Stand up slowly. Be careful on stairs.

description: Levothyroxine replaces the thyroid hormone (T4) that your body is not making enough of. It is the standard treatment for hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid) and is taken every day for life.
howItWorks: Levothyroxine is a synthetic version of the T4 hormone normally produced by your thyroid gland. Once absorbed, your body converts some of it to T3 (the active form). Together, T3 and T4 regulate your metabolism, energy, heart rate, and body temperature.

commonSideEffects.effect: Symptoms of too-high dose: palpitations, sweating, weight loss, anxiety
commonSideEffects.advice: Tell your doctor — the dose needs reducing. These are signs of excess thyroid hormone.
Usually settles once the right dose is found.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop palpitations, excessive sweating, unexplained weight changes, or persistent fatigue despite treatment. Regular blood tests (TSH) are essential to keep the dose correct.
storageInstructions: Store below 25°C. Protect from light and moisture. Take first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with a full glass of water. Wait 30-60 minutes before eating.

description: Carbimazole is an anti-thyroid medicine used to treat hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid), including Graves' disease. It reduces the amount of thyroid hormone your body produces.
howItWorks: Carbimazole is converted in your body to methimazole, which blocks an enzyme called thyroid peroxidase. This enzyme is essential for producing thyroid hormones T3 and T4. By blocking it, carbimazole gradually reduces hormone levels over 4-8 weeks.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food. Usually improves as your body adjusts.
Usually mild and temporary.
Tell your doctor. Usually mild but needs monitoring.

description: Tenofovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat chronic hepatitis B (and as part of HIV treatment). For hepatitis B, it suppresses the virus to prevent liver damage and cirrhosis.
howItWorks: Tenofovir blocks the hepatitis B virus from copying its DNA. It mimics a building block of DNA and, once incorporated, stops the DNA chain from growing further. This suppresses viral replication, allowing the liver to heal and reducing the risk of cirrhosis and liver cancer.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food. Symptoms usually improve within 2 weeks.
Usually mild and temporary.
Rest when needed. This often improves with time.

description: Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) is a bile acid used to treat primary biliary cholangitis, dissolve gallstones, and protect the liver in various chronic liver conditions.
howItWorks: UDCA replaces toxic bile acids in the liver with a non-toxic form. It protects liver cells from damage by these toxic bile acids, improves bile flow, and has anti-inflammatory properties. For gallstones, it gradually dissolves cholesterol stones over months.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food. Your doctor may adjust the dose.
Take with meals. Usually mild.
Taking with food helps.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe right-sided abdominal pain (possible gallstone complications)

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop worsening jaundice, severe abdominal pain, or increasing swelling. Regular liver function tests are needed to monitor treatment response.

description: Glimepiride is a sulfonylurea medication that helps lower blood sugar by stimulating your pancreas to produce more insulin. It is commonly used for type 2 diabetes when metformin alone is not enough.
howItWorks: Glimepiride binds to receptors on the insulin-producing beta cells in your pancreas, causing them to release more insulin into your bloodstream. This extra insulin helps move sugar from your blood into your cells where it is used for energy. It works best when taken with breakfast.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common, especially if meals are skipped
commonSideEffects.advice: Always eat regular meals. Carry glucose tablets or sweets. Symptoms include shakiness, sweating, and confusion.
Follow a balanced diet and stay physically active.
Take with food. Usually improves after the first few weeks.
Stand up slowly. Avoid driving if you feel dizzy.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe hypoglycaemia: confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness
seriousSideEffects.action: Give sugar immediately. If the person cannot swallow, call for emergency help.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Allergic reaction: skin rash, swelling, difficulty breathing

description: A fasting blood sugar test measures your blood glucose level after not eating for 8-12 hours. It is one of the most common tests for diagnosing and monitoring diabetes.

description: The OGTT is a diagnostic test where you drink a sugary solution and your blood sugar is measured at intervals. It shows how well your body handles a glucose load and is the gold standard for diagnosing gestational diabetes.
