seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe confusion or hallucinations
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor for dose adjustment.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Dramatically increases drowsiness and respiratory depression. Can be fatal.
Combined with opioids, greatly increases risk of respiratory depression.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek emergency help for very slow breathing, blue lips, or inability to wake someone taking morphine. Contact your doctor if pain is not controlled.
storageInstructions: Store safely out of reach of children and others. Extended-release tablets must not be crushed or chewed. Return unused morphine to a pharmacy for safe disposal.

description: Tramadol is a moderate-strength opioid painkiller used for cancer pain and other moderate to severe pain. It also has some antidepressant-like effects.
howItWorks: Tramadol works in two ways: it binds weakly to opioid receptors to reduce pain perception, and it inhibits the reuptake of serotonin and noradrenaline, which activates the body's own pain-suppression pathways. This dual action makes it effective for both nerve pain and tissue pain.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food.
Stand up slowly.
Drink plenty of water. A mild laxative may help.
Avoid driving if affected.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Seizures (rare, especially at high doses)
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help. Risk is higher in people with epilepsy.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Serotonin syndrome (when combined with antidepressants): confusion, fast heartbeat, high temperature
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help immediately.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: The combination can cause serotonin syndrome.
Increases drowsiness and risk of breathing problems.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek help for seizures, severe confusion, or breathing difficulties.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C. Keep away from children.

description: A CT (computed tomography) scan uses X-rays and a computer to create detailed cross-sectional images of your body. It is essential for cancer staging, monitoring treatment response, and diagnosing many conditions.
howItWorks: You lie on a table that moves through a ring-shaped scanner. The scanner takes many X-ray images from different angles around your body. A computer combines these into detailed cross-sectional images. A contrast dye may be injected to make certain structures more visible.

commonSideEffects.effect: Warm flushing sensation from contrast dye
commonSideEffects.advice: This passes within seconds and is normal.

commonSideEffects.effect: Metallic taste in mouth from contrast
commonSideEffects.advice: Temporary and harmless.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Allergic reaction to contrast dye (CT Scan): rash, swelling, breathing difficulty
seriousSideEffects.action: Tell the radiographer immediately. Emergency treatment is available.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Contrast dye can affect kidneys. Tell the team if you have kidney disease.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and next steps with you.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — these are performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A biopsy removes a small sample of tissue for examination under a microscope. It is the definitive way to diagnose cancer and determine its type and grade.
howItWorks: Depending on the location, a biopsy may be done with a needle (guided by ultrasound or CT), through an endoscope, or as a minor surgical procedure. The tissue sample is sent to a pathologist who examines the cells under a microscope to determine if cancer is present, what type it is, and how aggressive it is.

commonSideEffects.effect: Pain or discomfort at the biopsy site
commonSideEffects.advice: Local anaesthetic is used. Pain after the procedure is usually mild and manageable with paracetamol.
Apply gentle pressure. Report heavy bleeding to your doctor.
Ask your doctor about what to expect. A mild sedative may be offered.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Infection at the biopsy site: redness, swelling, fever
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor for antibiotics.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Significant bleeding that does not stop
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Tell your doctor about all medicines. Blood thinners may need to be paused before a biopsy to reduce bleeding risk.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and next steps with you.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — these are performed at healthcare facilities.

description: Tumour marker tests measure specific proteins in your blood that may be produced by cancer cells. They are used to monitor treatment response and check for cancer recurrence.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for specific proteins. Common markers include PSA (prostate), CA-125 (ovarian), CEA (bowel), CA 19-9 (pancreatic), and AFP (liver). Rising levels may indicate cancer growth, while falling levels suggest treatment is working. Markers are not used alone for diagnosis as they can be elevated in non-cancer conditions.

commonSideEffects.advice: The pain is momentary.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a standard blood test or monitoring procedure.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and next steps with you.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — these are performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A complete blood count with differential measures all types of blood cells. During cancer treatment, it monitors the effect of chemotherapy on your bone marrow.
howItWorks: A blood sample is analysed by a machine that counts red cells, white cells, and platelets, and identifies the different types of white cells (neutrophils, lymphocytes, etc.). During chemotherapy, this test shows when blood counts are at their lowest (nadir) and when they recover.

commonSideEffects.advice: The pain is momentary.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a standard blood test or monitoring procedure.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and next steps with you.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — these are performed at healthcare facilities.

description: Ferrous sulphate is an iron supplement used to treat anaemia, which is common in chronic kidney disease. It replaces the iron your body needs to make red blood cells.
howItWorks: Iron is a key component of haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. In kidney disease, anaemia develops because the kidneys produce less erythropoietin. Iron supplements ensure your body has enough raw material to make red blood cells when erythropoietin therapy is given.

commonSideEffects.advice: This is normal and harmless — it is just iron passing through.
Take with food if needed, though absorption is better on an empty stomach.
Drink plenty of water and eat high-fibre foods.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help for difficulty breathing or swelling.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Tea, coffee, or calcium supplements within 2 hours of iron
avoidanceWarnings.reason: These reduce iron absorption significantly. Take iron 2 hours apart from these.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if side effects are severe or if you develop new symptoms. For darbepoetin, report persistent headaches or leg swelling.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C.

description: Alfacalcidol is an active form of vitamin D used in kidney disease. Healthy kidneys activate vitamin D, but diseased kidneys cannot, leading to weak bones and calcium problems.
howItWorks: Alfacalcidol is already partially activated, bypassing the kidney step that fails in renal disease. It increases calcium absorption from food, strengthens bones, and helps control parathyroid hormone levels that rise dangerously in kidney disease.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food.
Usually mild.
Often related to underlying kidney disease rather than the medicine.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help for difficulty breathing or swelling.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if side effects are severe or if you develop new symptoms. For darbepoetin, report persistent headaches or leg swelling.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C.

description: Sodium bicarbonate tablets are used to correct the acid build-up (metabolic acidosis) that occurs when kidneys cannot excrete enough acid. It helps protect bones and slow kidney decline.
howItWorks: Healthy kidneys maintain the blood's acid-base balance. In kidney disease, acid accumulates. Sodium bicarbonate directly neutralises this excess acid, protecting bones (which dissolve in acidic conditions), reducing muscle wasting, and potentially slowing further kidney deterioration.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food.
Usually mild.
Often related to underlying kidney disease rather than the medicine.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help for difficulty breathing or swelling.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if side effects are severe or if you develop new symptoms. For darbepoetin, report persistent headaches or leg swelling.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C.

description: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate (Kayexalate) is used to lower dangerously high potassium levels in kidney disease. High potassium can cause fatal heart rhythm problems.
howItWorks: This resin exchanges sodium for potassium in the gut. When you swallow it, it passes through your intestines, binding potassium from your food and body fluids and carrying it out in your stool. Each dose can remove significant amounts of potassium.

commonSideEffects.advice: A laxative (sorbitol) is often given with it.
Mix with water or juice to improve the taste.
Tell your doctor if severe.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help for difficulty breathing or swelling.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if side effects are severe or if you develop new symptoms. For darbepoetin, report persistent headaches or leg swelling.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C.

description: Sevelamer is a phosphate binder taken with meals to prevent phosphate build-up in kidney disease. High phosphate causes dangerous calcium deposits in blood vessels and weakens bones.
howItWorks: When kidneys fail, they cannot excrete phosphate, causing levels to rise. Sevelamer binds to phosphate in the food you eat, trapping it in the gut so it passes out in stool instead of being absorbed into your blood. It must be taken with every meal to work.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with meals as directed.
Drink plenty of fluids.
Usually settles with continued use.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help for difficulty breathing or swelling.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Phosphate binders only work when taken with food. Missing a meal dose means that meal's phosphate enters your blood.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if side effects are severe or if you develop new symptoms. For darbepoetin, report persistent headaches or leg swelling.
storageInstructions: Store at room temperature below 30°C.

description: Darbepoetin is a long-acting injection that stimulates red blood cell production, treating the anaemia caused by kidney disease. It is given every 1-4 weeks.
howItWorks: Darbepoetin mimics erythropoietin, the hormone healthy kidneys produce to stimulate red blood cell production in bone marrow. Its modified structure gives it a longer duration than natural erythropoietin, so fewer injections are needed.

commonSideEffects.advice: Rotate injection sites.
Usually mild.
Tell your doctor if persistent.

seriousSideEffects.effect: High blood pressure: headache, vision changes
seriousSideEffects.action: Blood pressure is monitored. Report persistent headaches.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Blood clots: leg swelling, chest pain, breathlessness
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if side effects are severe or if you develop new symptoms. For darbepoetin, report persistent headaches or leg swelling.
storageInstructions: Store in the refrigerator (2-8°C). Do not freeze.

description: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) fluid is a sterile solution used in home dialysis. It is infused into your abdominal cavity through a catheter and uses the peritoneum as a natural filter to clean your blood.
howItWorks: The fluid contains glucose at various concentrations (1.5%, 2.5%, 4.25%). When infused into the abdomen, waste products and excess water from your blood pass through the peritoneal membrane into the fluid by osmosis and diffusion. After a dwell time (usually 4-8 hours), the used fluid is drained out, carrying waste with it.

commonSideEffects.advice: This improves as you get used to having fluid in your abdomen. Start with lower volumes.
The glucose in PD fluid is absorbed. Your dietitian can advise on managing calorie intake.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Peritonitis: cloudy drainage, abdominal pain, fever
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your PD team immediately. This is a serious infection that needs urgent antibiotics.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Catheter infection: redness, swelling, or pus at the catheter exit site
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your PD nurse for assessment and treatment.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Contamination during bag exchanges can introduce bacteria into the abdomen, causing peritonitis. Always follow strict hygiene procedures.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your PD team immediately for cloudy fluid, abdominal pain with fever, or any signs of infection at the catheter site.
storageInstructions: Store bags in a clean, dry area at room temperature. Check expiry dates. Never use a bag that is cloudy, damaged, or expired.

description: Haemodialysis is a treatment that uses a machine to filter waste products, excess salt, and water from your blood when your kidneys can no longer do this. Sessions typically last 3-4 hours, three times per week.
howItWorks: Blood is drawn from your arm through a fistula or catheter and pumped through a dialyser (artificial kidney). The dialyser contains thousands of tiny fibres with semipermeable walls. Waste products pass from blood through these walls into a cleaning fluid (dialysate), while clean blood is returned to your body.

commonSideEffects.effect: Low blood pressure during treatment: dizziness, nausea, cramps
commonSideEffects.advice: Tell the staff immediately. They can slow the fluid removal or give fluids.
Stretching helps. Staff may give saline. Limit fluid between sessions to reduce the amount removed.
Plan to rest after dialysis. Many people feel better the day after.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Fistula or catheter infection: redness, swelling, fever
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek medical help urgently. Bloodstream infections are serious.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Blood clotting in the fistula: loss of 'buzz' (thrill)
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your dialysis team immediately. The fistula may need urgent treatment.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Missing dialysis allows dangerous build-up of potassium, fluid, and waste products that can cause heart problems or death.

whenToSeekHelp: Never miss a dialysis session without medical advice. Seek emergency help for fever, chest pain, or severe breathlessness between sessions.
storageInstructions: Not applicable — haemodialysis is performed at a dialysis centre.

description: A urea (BUN) test measures the amount of urea nitrogen in your blood. Urea is a waste product from protein breakdown that healthy kidneys filter out.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for urea concentration. High levels indicate the kidneys are not filtering efficiently. The test is usually done alongside creatinine for a complete picture of kidney function. Normal blood urea is 2.5-7.1 mmol/L.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe, routine diagnostic tests.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss the results and any changes to your treatment plan.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: An electrolyte panel measures key minerals in your blood: sodium, potassium, chloride, and bicarbonate. These must be kept within narrow ranges for your heart and muscles to work properly.
howItWorks: A blood sample is analysed for four main electrolytes. In kidney disease, potassium often rises (dangerous for the heart), bicarbonate falls (causing acidosis), and sodium may be abnormal. The results guide medication choices and dietary advice.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe, routine diagnostic tests.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss the results and any changes to your treatment plan.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A kidney ultrasound creates images of your kidneys using sound waves. It shows kidney size, shape, and structure, and can detect blockages, stones, cysts, and tumours.
howItWorks: A probe coated in gel is placed on your skin over the kidney area. It emits high-frequency sound waves that bounce off kidney structures. The echoes are processed into images on a screen. The test is painless and takes about 20 minutes.

commonSideEffects.advice: The gel washes off easily.
Tell the sonographer if any area is tender.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe, routine diagnostic tests.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Full bladder may be requested for ultrasound
avoidanceWarnings.reason: A full bladder helps visualise the lower urinary tract. Drink water beforehand if instructed.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss the results and any changes to your treatment plan.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: Azithromycin is an antibiotic also used at low doses as a preventive treatment to reduce the frequency of COPD exacerbations (flare-ups).
howItWorks: At low doses, azithromycin has anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects beyond its antibiotic action. It reduces airway inflammation, decreases mucus production, and prevents bacterial colonisation of damaged airways. This reduces the frequency and severity of COPD flare-ups.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food. Usually settles within weeks.
Monitor your weight. Eat regular nutritious meals.
Usually mild and temporary.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe diarrhoea leading to dehydration
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor. You may need dose adjustment.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Heart rhythm changes (rare with long-term azithromycin)
seriousSideEffects.action: Your doctor will monitor with ECGs.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Can worsen stomach side effects.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop persistent diarrhoea, mood changes, or weight loss.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture.

description: Roflumilast is a PDE4 inhibitor tablet used for severe COPD with frequent exacerbations. It reduces airway inflammation through a different mechanism than steroids.
howItWorks: Roflumilast inhibits phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4), an enzyme that breaks down cyclic AMP in inflammatory cells. With more cyclic AMP, inflammatory cells become less active, reducing the chronic inflammation in COPD airways. It is used alongside bronchodilators and inhaled steroids.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food. Usually settles within weeks.
Monitor your weight. Eat regular nutritious meals.
Usually mild and temporary.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe diarrhoea leading to dehydration
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor. You may need dose adjustment.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Psychiatric effects: depression, insomnia, anxiety (roflumilast)
seriousSideEffects.action: Tell your doctor immediately if your mood changes.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Can worsen stomach side effects.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if you develop persistent diarrhoea, mood changes, or weight loss.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture.

description: An oxygen concentrator is a medical device that extracts and concentrates oxygen from room air, delivering it through a nasal cannula. It provides supplemental oxygen for people with severe COPD or other lung conditions.
howItWorks: Room air contains about 21% oxygen. The concentrator draws in room air, passes it through zeolite filters that trap nitrogen, and delivers concentrated oxygen (90-95% purity) through tubing to a nasal cannula or mask. It runs continuously on electricity.

commonSideEffects.advice: A humidifier bottle can be attached to the concentrator. Use water-based nasal gel.
Use soft ear cushions. Alternate between nasal cannula and mask.
Place on a mat to reduce vibration. Modern concentrators are quieter.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Oxygen toxicity from excessive flow rates: confusion, visual changes
seriousSideEffects.action: Never increase the flow rate above what your doctor prescribed.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Fire hazard: oxygen supports combustion
seriousSideEffects.action: Keep away from open flames, candles, and stoves. No smoking near oxygen equipment.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Smoking or open flames near the concentrator
avoidanceWarnings.reason: Oxygen dramatically increases fire risk. Never smoke while using oxygen. Keep away from cooking flames and candles.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your oxygen supplier if the concentrator is not working properly. Seek emergency help for worsening breathlessness despite oxygen use.
storageInstructions: Keep the concentrator in a well-ventilated room. Clean the external filter weekly. Keep away from walls (at least 15cm clearance on all sides). Have a backup power plan for outages.

description: Spirometry measures how much air you can breathe in and out, and how fast you can blow air out. It is the key test for diagnosing COPD and asthma and monitoring their severity.
howItWorks: You breathe into a mouthpiece connected to a spirometer, which measures airflow. The main measurements are FEV1 (how much air you blow out in the first second) and FVC (total amount you can blow out). The FEV1/FVC ratio distinguishes obstructive diseases (COPD, asthma) from restrictive ones.

commonSideEffects.advice: Rest between attempts. The technician will guide you through the breathing technique.
Sit down between attempts.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Bronchospasm triggered by spirometry (in severe asthma)
seriousSideEffects.action: A bronchodilator will be available. Tell staff about your asthma severity.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Using your inhaler before the test may mask the true severity of your airway obstruction. Follow your doctor's instructions about when to stop inhalers before testing.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will explain the results and what they mean for your treatment plan.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A sputum culture identifies bacteria or fungi in the mucus you cough up from your lungs. It helps choose the right antibiotic for chest infections.
howItWorks: You cough up a sample of sputum (not saliva) into a sterile container, ideally first thing in the morning. The lab grows any organisms present and tests which antibiotics they are sensitive to. Results usually take 2-5 days.

commonSideEffects.advice: Deep breathing or inhaling steam beforehand can help loosen sputum.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a simple specimen collection.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will explain the results and what they mean for your treatment plan.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: Propylthiouracil (PTU) blocks the production of thyroid hormones. It is used for hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid) and is preferred during the first trimester of pregnancy.
howItWorks: PTU works in two ways: it blocks the enzyme thyroid peroxidase, preventing iodine from being incorporated into thyroid hormones, and it blocks the conversion of T4 to the more active T3 in peripheral tissues. This double action makes it particularly effective for thyroid storm.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food.
Usually temporary.
Tell your doctor.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Liver damage (PTU): yellowing skin, dark urine, severe fatigue
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop taking PTU and seek emergency help. Liver function tests are needed.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Agranulocytosis: severe sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop the medicine and get an urgent blood test. This means very low white blood cells.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek immediate help for sore throat with fever (may indicate dangerously low white blood cells) or yellowing skin.
storageInstructions: Store PTU below 25°C. Store Lugol's in a dark bottle away from light.

description: Lugol's iodine is a potassium iodide solution used to reduce thyroid hormone release before thyroid surgery and during thyroid storm (emergency).
howItWorks: At high concentrations, iodine paradoxically suppresses thyroid hormone production and release (the Wolff-Chaikoff effect). It also reduces blood flow to the thyroid gland, making surgery safer. The effect is temporary (1-2 weeks), so it is only used short-term before surgery.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food.
Mix Lugol's with juice or milk to mask the taste.
Tell your doctor.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Iodine allergy: rash, swelling, breathing difficulty
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help if you are allergic to iodine.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Agranulocytosis: severe sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers
seriousSideEffects.action: Stop the medicine and get an urgent blood test. This means very low white blood cells.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Prolonged iodine use can paradoxically worsen thyroid problems.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek immediate help for sore throat with fever (may indicate dangerously low white blood cells) or yellowing skin.
storageInstructions: Store in a dark glass bottle at room temperature. Protect from light.

description: Radioactive iodine therapy uses iodine-131 to destroy overactive thyroid tissue. It is a one-time treatment that provides a permanent solution for hyperthyroidism.
howItWorks: You swallow a capsule or liquid containing radioactive iodine-131. Because the thyroid gland actively absorbs iodine, the radioactivity is concentrated in the thyroid. The radiation destroys overactive thyroid cells over weeks to months. Eventually, most patients need thyroid hormone replacement.

commonSideEffects.effect: Temporary neck swelling or tenderness after RAI
commonSideEffects.advice: This means the treatment is working. Take pain relief if needed.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid) after RAI — expected outcome
seriousSideEffects.action: You will need lifelong thyroid hormone replacement (levothyroxine). This is expected, not a complication.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Radioactive iodine can harm the developing baby or pass through breast milk. A pregnancy test is done before treatment.

whenToSeekHelp: For RAI, you will need to follow radiation safety precautions for a few days after treatment. Your nuclear medicine team will give specific instructions.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — these are performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A thyroid ultrasound uses sound waves to create images of the thyroid gland in your neck. It detects nodules, enlargement, and other structural abnormalities.
howItWorks: A gel-coated probe is placed on the front of your neck. Sound waves create real-time images of the thyroid. The test can measure the gland's size, detect nodules (solid or fluid-filled), and guide needle biopsies if needed.

commonSideEffects.advice: The gel washes off easily.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a safe, routine test.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and any further testing needed.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — these are performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A T3/T4 test measures thyroid hormone levels in your blood. Combined with TSH, these tests diagnose and monitor thyroid disorders — both overactive and underactive thyroid.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for Free T3 (triiodothyronine) and Free T4 (thyroxine) — the active thyroid hormones. Free T4 is the main hormone produced by the thyroid; T3 is the more active form converted from T4. High levels indicate hyperthyroidism; low levels indicate hypothyroidism.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a safe, routine test.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and any further testing needed.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — these are performed at healthcare facilities.

description: Dipyridamole is an antiplatelet medicine used to prevent blood clots after stroke or TIA (mini-stroke). It is often combined with low-dose aspirin for enhanced protection.
howItWorks: Dipyridamole inhibits phosphodiesterase enzymes and blocks the reuptake of adenosine in blood platelets. This increases cyclic AMP levels in platelets, making them less 'sticky' and less likely to form clots. The combination with aspirin provides better stroke prevention than either drug alone.

commonSideEffects.advice: Usually settles within days. Start with a low dose and increase gradually.
Stand up slowly.
Take with food.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe bleeding: bruising, blood in stool or urine
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek medical help.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe drop in blood pressure: fainting
seriousSideEffects.action: Lie down and call for help.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Increases the risk of bleeding and dizziness.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek medical help for severe headache, bleeding, or signs of a new stroke (face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty).
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C.

description: Nimodipine is a calcium channel blocker specifically used to prevent brain blood vessel spasm (vasospasm) after subarachnoid haemorrhage — a type of bleeding stroke.
howItWorks: Nimodipine preferentially acts on brain blood vessels, blocking calcium entry into the smooth muscle cells of cerebral arteries. This prevents the severe narrowing (vasospasm) that commonly occurs 4-14 days after subarachnoid haemorrhage and can cause further brain damage.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take a mild painkiller.
Stand up slowly.
Take with food.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe headache (with nimodipine: may indicate worsening vasospasm)
seriousSideEffects.action: Report to your medical team immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe drop in blood pressure: fainting
seriousSideEffects.action: Lie down and call for help.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Can increase nimodipine levels dangerously.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek medical help for severe headache, bleeding, or signs of a new stroke (face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty).
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C.

description: Enoxaparin (Clexane) is a low-molecular-weight heparin injection that prevents and treats blood clots. It is used after stroke, surgery, and during hospitalisation.
howItWorks: Enoxaparin activates antithrombin III, a natural anticoagulant protein. This blocks Factor Xa and thrombin in the clotting cascade, preventing blood clots from forming or growing. It is given as a subcutaneous (under the skin) injection, usually in the abdomen.

commonSideEffects.advice: Rotate injection sites. Do not rub the site after injecting.

commonSideEffects.effect: Bleeding from minor cuts taking longer to stop
commonSideEffects.advice: Apply pressure for longer than usual.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe bleeding: blood in urine, black stools, coughing blood
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help immediately.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia: a paradoxical clotting disorder
seriousSideEffects.action: Blood platelet counts are monitored. Report any new pain or swelling.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk when combined with blood thinners.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek medical help for severe headache, bleeding, or signs of a new stroke (face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty).
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C. Enoxaparin: store below 25°C, do not freeze.

description: Alteplase (tPA) is a clot-dissolving drug given within 4.5 hours of an acute ischaemic stroke to restore blood flow to the brain. It is a life-saving emergency treatment.
howItWorks: Alteplase is a recombinant tissue plasminogen activator. It converts plasminogen (an inactive protein in the blood) into plasmin, which actively breaks down the fibrin mesh holding the blood clot together. As the clot dissolves, blood flow to the brain is restored.

commonSideEffects.effect: Bleeding from injection sites or gums
commonSideEffects.advice: Staff will monitor closely. Apply pressure to any bleeding.
Anti-sickness medicines can be given.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe bleeding: into the brain, gastrointestinal, or other sites
seriousSideEffects.action: This is closely monitored in hospital. Emergency treatment is immediately available.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Allergic reaction: rash, swelling, breathing difficulty
seriousSideEffects.action: Emergency treatment is available in the stroke unit.

whenToSeekHelp: Alteplase is given in a hospital emergency setting with continuous monitoring.
storageInstructions: Alteplase is stored and administered in hospital.

description: A CT brain scan uses X-rays to create detailed images of the brain. In stroke, it is the first imaging test performed to distinguish between a bleed (haemorrhagic) and a blockage (ischaemic) — a critical distinction that determines treatment.
howItWorks: You lie on a table that slides into the CT scanner ring. The scan takes only a few minutes. In stroke, a CT can immediately show bleeding (appearing white) but may not show an ischaemic stroke for several hours. Treatment decisions are based on the scan plus clinical assessment.

commonSideEffects.advice: The test or session is painless.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant medical risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

whenToSeekHelp: Results of imaging tests are usually available within hours. Rehabilitation sessions are ongoing — attend all scheduled appointments for the best recovery.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: MRI brain uses powerful magnets and radio waves to create detailed images of brain structure. It is more sensitive than CT for detecting strokes, especially small or early ones.
howItWorks: You lie inside a large magnet while radio waves are pulsed through your brain. Different brain tissues respond differently, creating highly detailed images. Diffusion-weighted MRI can detect ischaemic stroke within minutes of onset, making it more sensitive than CT.

commonSideEffects.advice: Tell staff beforehand. Open MRI machines or sedation may be available.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant medical risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Some metal implants are not safe in the MRI scanner. Tell your team about any implants, pacemakers, or metal fragments.

whenToSeekHelp: Results of imaging tests are usually available within hours. Rehabilitation sessions are ongoing — attend all scheduled appointments for the best recovery.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A carotid Doppler ultrasound examines the arteries in your neck that supply blood to the brain. Narrowing of these arteries is a major cause of stroke.
howItWorks: A gel-coated probe is placed on your neck. Sound waves bounce off blood cells flowing through the carotid arteries. The Doppler effect measures the speed of blood flow — faster flow indicates narrowing. The test can detect plaque build-up and measure the degree of blockage.

commonSideEffects.advice: The test or session is painless.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant medical risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

howItWorks: A speech-language pathologist assesses your specific difficulties and designs a tailored rehabilitation programme. This may include exercises for tongue and mouth muscles, word-finding practice, comprehension exercises, swallowing techniques, and alternative communication strategies.

commonSideEffects.advice: The test or session is painless.

howItWorks: An occupational therapist assesses what daily activities are difficult and designs a rehabilitation programme. This includes exercises to improve arm and hand function, techniques to compensate for weakness, home modifications, and cognitive rehabilitation. The goal is maximum independence.

description: Lactulose is a synthetic sugar used to prevent and treat hepatic encephalopathy — confusion caused by toxin build-up when the liver cannot filter properly. It also treats constipation.
howItWorks: In the colon, bacteria break lactulose into acids that lower the gut pH. This traps ammonia (a toxic waste product normally cleared by the liver) in the gut and draws water into the bowel, flushing ammonia out in loose stools. Reducing ammonia levels protects the brain.

commonSideEffects.frequency: Common — dose is adjusted to produce 2-3 soft stools daily
commonSideEffects.advice: The goal is slightly loose stools. Tell your doctor if diarrhoea is severe.
Mix with juice or water.
Usually improves as your body adjusts.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe dehydration from excessive diarrhoea: extreme thirst, dizziness, reduced urination
seriousSideEffects.action: Contact your doctor to adjust the dose. Drink plenty of fluids.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Stopping lactulose can cause rapid ammonia build-up and confusion within days.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if confusion worsens, diarrhoea is severe, or you develop new symptoms.
storageInstructions: Store lactulose below 25°C (do not freeze). Store rifaximin below 30°C.

description: Rifaximin is a non-absorbable antibiotic used alongside lactulose to prevent recurring hepatic encephalopathy. It is not absorbed into the bloodstream, so it works only in the gut.
howItWorks: Rifaximin kills ammonia-producing bacteria in the gut. Since it is barely absorbed, it stays in the intestines where it is needed. With fewer bacteria producing ammonia, less ammonia enters the bloodstream and reaches the brain. Combined with lactulose, it significantly reduces encephalopathy episodes.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food.
Usually mild.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help for difficulty breathing or swelling.

whenToSeekHelp: Contact your doctor if confusion worsens, diarrhoea is severe, or you develop new symptoms.
storageInstructions: Store lactulose below 25°C (do not freeze). Store rifaximin below 30°C.

description: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting. In liver disease, the liver cannot produce enough clotting factors, and vitamin K supplements help restore some clotting ability.
howItWorks: The liver uses vitamin K to produce clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X. In liver disease, production of these factors drops, increasing bleeding risk. Supplemental vitamin K provides the raw material for whatever clotting factor production the liver can still manage.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food.
Usually mild.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help for difficulty breathing or swelling.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek help for signs of allergic reaction or unusual bleeding.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C.

description: Intravenous albumin is a protein infusion used for serious complications of liver cirrhosis, including spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, large-volume paracentesis, and hepatorenal syndrome.
howItWorks: Albumin is the main protein in blood, responsible for maintaining fluid balance. In cirrhosis, the liver produces less albumin, causing fluid to leak out of blood vessels into the abdomen (ascites) and tissues. IV albumin temporarily restores blood volume and organ perfusion.

commonSideEffects.advice: The infusion rate can be slowed.
Tell the nurse. Slowing the infusion usually helps.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help for difficulty breathing or swelling.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek help for signs of allergic reaction or unusual bleeding.
storageInstructions: IV albumin is stored and administered in hospital.

description: The hepatitis B vaccine provides immunity against the hepatitis B virus, preventing chronic liver infection, cirrhosis, and liver cancer.
howItWorks: The vaccine contains a surface protein (HBsAg) of the hepatitis B virus, produced in yeast cells. When injected, your immune system recognises this protein as foreign and creates antibodies and memory cells. If you later encounter the real virus, your immune system destroys it before infection can establish.

commonSideEffects.advice: Apply a cold pack. Move your arm to reduce stiffness.
Take paracetamol if needed.
Rest for a day. This is a normal immune response.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help for difficulty breathing or swelling.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek help for signs of allergic reaction or unusual bleeding.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C.

description: An abdominal ultrasound uses sound waves to image the liver, gallbladder, spleen, and other organs. It detects liver size changes, cirrhosis, ascites, gallstones, and liver tumours.
howItWorks: A gel-coated probe is moved across your abdomen. Sound waves bounce off internal organs and create real-time images on a screen. It can show liver texture (normal, fatty, or cirrhotic), measure liver size, detect fluid in the abdomen, and identify masses.

commonSideEffects.advice: Minimal discomfort.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe, routine diagnostic tests.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Eating before ultrasound (if fasting is requested)
avoidanceWarnings.reason: A full stomach can obscure the gallbladder and liver. Follow fasting instructions if given.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and any follow-up needed.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a blood test used to screen for liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma) in people with cirrhosis. Rising levels may indicate early cancer.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for AFP, a protein normally produced during fetal development. In adults, high AFP levels can indicate liver cancer, though some benign conditions also raise it. People with cirrhosis should have AFP checked every 6 months for early cancer detection.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe, routine diagnostic tests.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and any follow-up needed.

description: The HBsAg test detects the surface protein of the hepatitis B virus in your blood. A positive result confirms active or chronic hepatitis B infection.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for the hepatitis B surface antigen. If present, it means the virus is actively reproducing in your body. In acute infection, HBsAg appears within weeks of exposure. If it persists for more than 6 months, you have chronic hepatitis B.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe, routine diagnostic tests.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and any follow-up needed.

description: The anti-HCV test detects antibodies to the hepatitis C virus. A positive result means you have been exposed to the virus and need a confirmatory test.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for antibodies your immune system made against hepatitis C. A positive result means exposure but does not distinguish between current and past infection. If positive, an HCV RNA test confirms whether the virus is still active.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe, routine diagnostic tests.

description: A Fibroscan (transient elastography) measures liver stiffness, which correlates with the degree of fibrosis (scarring). It is a non-invasive alternative to liver biopsy.
howItWorks: A probe is placed on your right side between your ribs. It sends a low-frequency vibration into the liver and measures how fast the wave travels. Stiffer liver (more scarring) transmits the wave faster. The result is given in kilopascals (kPa) — higher values indicate more fibrosis.

commonSideEffects.advice: Minimal discomfort.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe, routine diagnostic tests.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: A recent meal increases liver blood flow, which can give falsely high stiffness readings.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss results and any follow-up needed.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: Penicillin V is a prophylactic antibiotic given daily to children and adults with sickle cell disease to prevent life-threatening pneumococcal infections.
howItWorks: Sickle cell disease damages the spleen, which normally filters bacteria from the blood. Without a functioning spleen, pneumococcal bacteria can cause overwhelming infection (sepsis) within hours. Daily penicillin provides a constant antibiotic barrier against these bacteria.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take with food.
Usually temporary.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction to penicillin: rash, swelling, breathing difficulty
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help. An alternative antibiotic will be prescribed.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Even one missed day can leave you vulnerable to overwhelming infection. Set a daily reminder.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek immediate help for fever above 38°C (may indicate serious infection in sickle cell disease), severe pain crisis, or signs of allergic reaction.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C.

description: L-Glutamine (Endari) is an amino acid supplement that reduces the frequency of sickle cell pain crises by protecting red blood cells from oxidative damage.
howItWorks: Sickle red blood cells are prone to oxidative stress, which causes them to sickle and clump. L-Glutamine increases the production of NAD+, a molecule that protects cells from oxidative damage. With less oxidative stress, red blood cells sickle less often, reducing pain crises.

commonSideEffects.advice: Drink plenty of water.
Take with food.
Usually mild.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Severe allergic reaction
seriousSideEffects.action: Seek emergency help.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek immediate help for fever above 38°C (may indicate serious infection in sickle cell disease), severe pain crisis, or signs of allergic reaction.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C.

description: Deferasirox is an iron chelator (binder) used to remove excess iron from the body in people who receive regular blood transfusions. Without chelation, iron accumulates and damages organs.
howItWorks: Each unit of transfused blood contains about 250mg of iron, but the body has no mechanism to excrete excess iron. Deferasirox binds to iron in the bloodstream and tissues, forming a complex that is excreted in stool. This prevents iron from depositing in the heart, liver, and endocrine organs.

commonSideEffects.advice: Take on an empty stomach or as directed. Usually improves over time.
Tell your doctor. Mild rashes may resolve.
Take at the same time daily. Report persistent pain.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Kidney damage: reduced urination, swelling
seriousSideEffects.action: Your doctor monitors kidney function monthly.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Liver problems: yellowing skin, dark urine
seriousSideEffects.action: Liver function is monitored regularly.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: These reduce deferasirox absorption. Take 2 hours apart.

whenToSeekHelp: Seek immediate help for fever above 38°C (may indicate serious infection in sickle cell disease), severe pain crisis, or signs of allergic reaction.
storageInstructions: Store below 30°C.

description: Blood transfusion in sickle cell disease replaces sickle red blood cells with healthy donor cells. It treats severe anaemia, prevents stroke, and manages acute crises.
howItWorks: Healthy donor blood (matched for compatibility) is given through a vein over 2-4 hours. In sickle cell disease, transfusion both increases oxygen-carrying capacity and dilutes the proportion of sickle cells. Exchange transfusion removes sickle blood while replacing it with healthy blood.

commonSideEffects.effect: Mild fever or chills during transfusion
commonSideEffects.advice: Tell the nurse. The transfusion can be slowed and medicines given.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Transfusion reaction: fever, rash, breathing difficulty
seriousSideEffects.action: Tell the nurse immediately. The transfusion will be stopped and treatment given.

whenToSeekHelp: For transfusions, tell the nurse immediately about any fever, itching, rash, or breathing difficulty. For TCD, your doctor will discuss the results and what they mean for stroke prevention.
storageInstructions: Not applicable — these are hospital-based procedures or vaccines stored by the pharmacy.

description: The pneumococcal vaccine protects against Streptococcus pneumoniae, a bacterium that is especially dangerous for people with sickle cell disease due to their impaired spleen function.
howItWorks: The vaccine exposes your immune system to parts of the pneumococcal bacterial capsule. Your body creates antibodies and memory cells. If you encounter the real bacteria, your immune system can rapidly destroy them before they cause serious infection.

commonSideEffects.advice: Apply a cold pack.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks

description: A reticulocyte count measures young red blood cells in your blood. In sickle cell disease, it shows how hard your bone marrow is working to replace destroyed sickle cells.
howItWorks: A blood sample is analysed for reticulocytes — immature red blood cells released early from bone marrow. In sickle cell disease, the normal count is higher than average because the bone marrow is constantly replacing destroyed sickle cells. Changes in the count help monitor disease activity.

commonSideEffects.effect: Brief needle discomfort or no discomfort
commonSideEffects.advice: Minimal discomfort.

description: Haemoglobin electrophoresis separates and identifies different types of haemoglobin in your blood. It is the definitive test for diagnosing sickle cell disease and trait.
howItWorks: A blood sample is placed on a gel and an electrical current is applied. Different haemoglobin types (HbA, HbS, HbC, HbF) move at different speeds through the gel, creating a pattern. Sickle cell disease shows predominantly HbS; sickle trait shows both HbA and HbS.

commonSideEffects.effect: Brief needle discomfort or no discomfort
commonSideEffects.advice: Minimal discomfort.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks

description: Transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasound measures blood flow velocity in brain arteries. In children with sickle cell disease, it identifies those at high risk of stroke.
howItWorks: A probe is placed on the temples and back of the head. Ultrasound waves pass through thin skull bone to measure blood flow speed in brain arteries. Higher velocities indicate narrowing, which in sickle cell disease means higher stroke risk. Children with high velocities start regular transfusions.

commonSideEffects.effect: Brief needle discomfort or no discomfort
commonSideEffects.advice: Minimal discomfort.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: These are safe diagnostic tests or standard vaccinations.

description: A CD4 count measures the number of CD4 T-cells in your blood. These immune cells are the primary target of HIV, and their count indicates how well your immune system is functioning.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for CD4+ T-lymphocytes using flow cytometry. Normal CD4 count is 500-1500 cells/μL. Below 200 indicates severe immune suppression (AIDS). The test helps decide when to start treatment and monitors immune recovery on ARVs.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a standard blood test.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss your CD4 count and what it means for your treatment plan.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A viral load test measures the amount of HIV RNA in your blood. It is the key test for monitoring whether your ARV treatment is working — the goal is an undetectable viral load.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested using PCR (polymerase chain reaction) technology to count HIV RNA copies. An undetectable viral load (below 50 copies/mL) means the virus is fully suppressed and you cannot transmit HIV sexually. Detectable levels may mean medication is not working or adherence needs improvement.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a standard blood test.

whenToSeekHelp: A detectable viral load on treatment needs discussion with your doctor about adherence or possible drug resistance.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A creatinine test measures creatinine in your blood, a waste product from normal muscle activity. Your kidneys filter creatinine, so high levels indicate the kidneys are not working properly.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for creatinine. The level, combined with your age, sex, and weight, is used to calculate eGFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate), which shows your percentage of kidney function. Normal creatinine is approximately 60-110 μmol/L for men and 45-90 μmol/L for women.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a standard blood test.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: Intense exercise can temporarily raise creatinine levels, giving a falsely abnormal result.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will explain what your creatinine and eGFR mean for your kidney health.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A full blood count (FBC or CBC) measures red cells, white cells, and platelets in your blood. It is one of the most commonly ordered blood tests and helps diagnose anaemia, infections, and blood disorders.
howItWorks: A blood sample is analysed by an automated machine that counts and classifies blood cells. Key results include haemoglobin (oxygen-carrying capacity), white blood cell count (infection fighting), and platelet count (clotting). In sickle cell disease, it monitors anaemia severity and overall blood health.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a standard blood test.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will discuss your results and any changes to your treatment.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: Liver function tests (LFTs) measure enzymes and proteins produced by the liver. They help diagnose liver disease, monitor treatment, and detect medication side effects on the liver.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for several markers: ALT and AST (liver enzymes that rise when liver cells are damaged), ALP and GGT (enzymes that rise with bile duct problems), bilirubin (the yellow pigment that causes jaundice when high), and albumin (a protein the liver produces). Together they paint a picture of liver health.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a standard blood test.

avoidanceWarnings.substance: Alcohol within 24 hours of the test
avoidanceWarnings.reason: Recent alcohol can temporarily elevate liver enzymes, giving misleading results.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will explain which values are abnormal and what they mean. Mildly elevated enzymes are common and may not indicate serious disease.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.

description: A peak flow test measures how fast you can blow air out of your lungs. It is a simple, quick test used to monitor asthma control and detect early signs of worsening.
howItWorks: You take a deep breath and blow as hard and fast as possible into a small handheld device (peak flow meter). The meter measures your peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) in litres per minute. Your personal best reading becomes your reference. A drop below 80% suggests worsening asthma; below 50% is an emergency.

commonSideEffects.effect: Brief breathlessness or cough after blowing
commonSideEffects.advice: Rest between attempts. Three readings are taken and the best is recorded.

seriousSideEffects.effect: Dizziness from forceful blowing
seriousSideEffects.action: Sit down and rest. This is mild and passes quickly.

whenToSeekHelp: Track your peak flow readings daily as instructed. Seek help if readings drop significantly below your personal best.
storageInstructions: Keep your peak flow meter clean and dry. Replace the mouthpiece as recommended by the manufacturer.

description: Physiotherapy after stroke helps restore movement, strength, balance, and coordination. It is a critical part of stroke rehabilitation that should begin as soon as possible after the stroke.
howItWorks: A physiotherapist assesses your movement difficulties and designs a tailored exercise programme. This may include strengthening exercises, balance training, gait (walking) retraining, stretching to prevent contractures, and functional exercises for daily tasks. The brain can form new pathways (neuroplasticity) to compensate for damaged areas.

commonSideEffects.advice: This is normal and shows you are working the right muscles. Gentle stretching and rest help.
Pace yourself. Recovery takes energy.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant medical risks
seriousSideEffects.action: Exercises are tailored to your ability level and progressed safely.

whenToSeekHelp: Attend all scheduled sessions for the best recovery outcomes. Tell your physiotherapist about any new pain or worsening symptoms.
storageInstructions: Not applicable — physiotherapy sessions are conducted at healthcare facilities or at home with a therapist.

description: A thyroid function test measures TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) and thyroid hormones to diagnose and monitor thyroid disorders. TSH is the single most important thyroid test.
howItWorks: A blood sample is tested for TSH and usually Free T4. TSH is produced by the pituitary gland and tells the thyroid how much hormone to make. High TSH means the thyroid is underactive (hypothyroidism); low TSH means it is overactive (hyperthyroidism). Free T4 confirms the diagnosis.

commonSideEffects.advice: Momentary pain only.

seriousSideEffects.effect: No significant risks
seriousSideEffects.action: This is a standard blood test.

avoidanceWarnings.reason: High-dose biotin can interfere with thyroid test results, giving falsely abnormal readings. Stop biotin 2-3 days before testing.

whenToSeekHelp: Your doctor will interpret your TSH and thyroid hormone levels together with your symptoms to guide treatment.
storageInstructions: No storage needed — performed at healthcare facilities.
